- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment periods.
- After a sharp spike in price (forecast > 10x historical mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33); apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: average sentiment over last 5 days to adjust forecast mean.
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 1.80), model tends to overpredict; apply 1.5x decay factor to forecast for 3–5 days post-reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive and price is rising, model often fails to capture long-term momentum; add 5–10% buffer to forecast for sustained positive sentiment.
